A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Earth-Agent framework and Earth-Bench benchmark. The main text and appendices support reliable comparison; rasterized appendix figures in v3 were inspected visually, and relocated material was matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original Earth-Bench evaluations, comparisons with general agents and remote-sensing MLLMs, tool-use ablations, and error analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds an RGB input control, latency measurements, and analyses relating accuracy to tool-call counts.

M1.justification: The perception toolkit replaces count_skeleton_contours, described as applying erosion and skeletonization before counting contours, with count_connected_components, described as counting connected components directly. This revision also appears in change-detection traces. The ReAct/MCP controller and overall toolkit organization remain unchanged; the expanded batching discussion documents functionality already present in v1.

E1.justification: The broad benchmark coverage remains three modalities and 14 task types, with the same external evaluation datasets. However, the Lake Geneva example changes from NDWI-based water coverage to NDVI-based vegetation analysis (v1 Figures 22–23; v3 Figures 24–25), revising the task requirements. The new source-composition table otherwise documents existing coverage rather than establishing added datasets.

E2.justification: The external comparators remain GPT-Agent, MGX, Manus, and Coze in Table 2, and the same six MLLMs in Table 3. The added Earth-Agent(Kimik2) row extends evaluation of the proposed framework's configurations rather than introducing an external comparison method.

E3.justification: v3 adds base64-encoded RGB inputs as a control in the no-tool ablation, evaluates the Kimi-K2 configuration on Earth-Bench-Lite, and introduces elapsed-time measurements and accuracy stratification by total and unique tool-call counts. Existing dual-level metrics and AP/IF regimes are retained. Newly described dataset curation does not establish a changed split or rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendices E–F substantially extend the analyses with LLM-versus-tool latency breakdowns and accuracy versus total and unique tool usage. Appendix A.6 strengthens the no-tool ablation with actual RGB image inputs. Several case studies are revised, including replacing v1's duplicated drought panel with a temperature-monitoring IF trace; the Shanghai building-volume IF example is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental random seeds, confidence intervals, or uncertainty estimates for benchmark performance. The new question-count strata and bubble sizes describe sample distributions, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial latency, scaling, and RGB-control results. Table 2 adds Earth-Agent(Kimik2) with 45.95 average accuracy. Table 1 revises existing scores, including GPT-5 AP accuracy from 65.59 to 65.99 and Gemini-2.5 from 54.66 to 52.23, while Appendix C's modality scores remain unchanged. Case answers, trajectories, and some efficiency values also change; revised tasks do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, trajectory factorization, and six evaluation equations in Appendix B.2 are retained. The new analyses and implementation example introduce no new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: an MCP/ReAct framework with 104 tools, a multimodal Earth-Bench with trajectory and outcome evaluation, and advantages over general agents and remote-sensing MLLMs. Added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations that model calls dominate latency, batching can reduce interactions, and excessive tool usage exposes limitations in long-chain reasoning. It also argues that accuracy benefits justify computational cost and discusses the RGB input control. Existing modality-specific limitations and error-mechanism interpretations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands reproducibility information through sensor/product counts, task distributions, annotator roles, screening criteria, and input-band annotations. It adds NDVI batching implementation code, repository/dataset/project links, and a commitment to provide evaluation logs. v1 supplied tool descriptions and an LST code example but only promised a future code/data release.

R1.justification: v3 adds Wang et al.'s work on realistic Earth-observation constellation scheduling to the introduction and references. The related-work discussion and positioning against earlier EO agents and MLLMs otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained. v3 expands and subdivides the appendices, adds ethics, reproducibility, and acknowledgement statements, updates affiliation/header information, and clarifies several example queries. These are localized expansions rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 adds composition, task-distribution, latency, and scaling tables plus three scaling plots. It reorders performance-table columns, revises Figures 4 and 6, adds band/count annotations to numerous examples, and redesigns the general-agent case gallery into horizontal panels. These substantive display changes extend beyond pagination and numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency and diagnostic value through curation details, access links, an RGB-input control, and latency/scaling evidence absent from v1. It also corrects some example annotations. The overall gain is limited by unexplained Table 1 revisions alongside unchanged modality tables and remaining inconsistencies in case-study traces, which prevent the additions from establishing a substantial improvement in evidential reliability.
